figures.finding: A child (under sixteen) may not be employed, save in artistic performances approved by the Minister on conditions he sets after consulting employers' and employees' organisations where practicable, or in Minister-approved light work from fourteen; a parent or guardian is liable for a child's unlawful employment unless it happened without his knowledge or consent. A young person (sixteen and seventeen) must pass a medical examination (repeated every six months), may not work in school hours while of compulsory school age without the education Minister's written consent, nor at night (20:00 to 05:00).

value.permit: the Minister's approval of the artistic performance
value.conditions: set by the Minister after consultation
value.reachesWritingDirecting: no: the exception is for artistic performances

figures.applies: British Virgin Islands; Labour Code Act 2010 ss. 128-130 as served; the 2020 amendment not read.

sources.said: artistic performances approved by the Minister and subject to conditions determined by the Minister after consultation with employers’ and employees’ representative organisations, where practicable;
the parent or guardian of that child is deemed to have committed an offence unless he or she proves that the employment occurred without his or her knowledge, consent, acquiescence or connivance
A person shall not, without the prior written consent of the Minister responsible for education, employ during school hours, a young person who is within the compulsory school age.
performed between the hours of 8:00 p.m. on one day and 5:00 a.m. on the following day.

sources.title: Labour Code Act, 2010 (No. 4 of 2010), Virgin Islands Laws Online (Attorney General's Chambers)
sources.said: artistic performances approved by the Minister and subject to conditions determined by the Minister after consultation with employers’ and employees’ representative organisations, where practicable; … the parent or guardian of that child is deemed to have committed an offence unless he or she proves that the employment occurred without his or her knowledge, consent, acquiescence or connivance … A person shall not, without the prior written consent of the Minister responsible for education, employ during school hours, a young person who is within the compulsory school age. … performed between the hours of 8:00 p.m. on one day and 5:00 a.m. on the following day.
